kicker: Good carvers don't remember everything — they hang each tool in its place.
summary: Don't remind AI every day — teach it once, hang it in the right place, call it when needed.

quiz.q: Every Monday you retype the same long instructions so AI writes the weekly report. What is the most sensible upgrade?
options: Type faster, or paste from your notes
Package the instructions as a skill with a clear “when to use”
Let an agent send the report on its own, no review
Switch to the most expensive model
quiz.explain: A skill keeps the instructions in one place, and AI opens it when the task fits. Sending things out should still wait for your approval.

ladder.label: The automation stairs
ladder.art: Ink painting: five dry-stone terraces zig-zag left and right up a mossy hillside, earth banks and bands of mist between them, a pine wood behind and the moon over the workshop roof. Each terrace has a stone lantern and a dressed stone carved with its name; when you arrive the lantern lights, a warm pool spreads on the moss and its little scene plays: a request said once thins into mist, a scroll hangs in a stone niche, a paper figure hops across stones by itself, a bamboo trough runs through three gates and waits for a seal, a shishi-odoshi tips and knocks on its own.
ladder.sealAria: Vermilion seal: approve so the workflow runs on

rungs.name: Prompt
rungs.what: Say it once, then it's forgotten. Next time you explain from scratch.
rungs.example: Every Monday you type: “summarise this week's numbers using the template…”

rungs.name: Skill
rungs.what: A packaged instruction sheet; AI opens it by itself when the task fits.
rungs.example: A “weekly report” skill: which columns, which tone, which template.

rungs.name: Agent
rungs.what: Does several steps by itself and picks its own tools.
rungs.example: Opens the spreadsheet, works out the changes, writes a draft.

rungs.name: Workflow
rungs.what: Steps chained along a fixed route, with checkpoints.
rungs.example: Get numbers → agent writes → you review → send.

rungs.name: Hook / schedule
rungs.what: Starts by itself at a set time or on an event.
rungs.example: 8 a.m. Monday, the workflow runs and waits for your review.

scale.text: This five-step ladder is AI Zen's own picture to make it easy to imagine, not a standard classification.

facts.text: Anthropic draws a line: workflows follow routes laid down in code; agents decide their own steps and tools.
A hook in Claude Code is a command that runs at a set moment, so it always happens rather than waiting for AI to remember.

insight.text: Which step is enough? Common advice: pick the simplest way that does the job; add complexity only when truly needed.

ladder.detail: Higher steps are handier but harder to control. Many jobs need just one good skill; workflows and schedules suit regular, repeated, stable work.

scroll.label: Unrolling a skill
scroll.art: Ink painting: a dark wall of boards in an alcove, a round window letting in a dusty shaft of moonlight. Nine skill scrolls hang from a bamboo rail, each its own length, silk and knob. A hand-held paper lantern is the key light: only inside its pool can the name tags be read. Open the readable one and the paper unrolls sideways along the wall as a makimono (on a phone it hangs down as a kakemono), notes in vermilion in the margin, a copy seal at its tail, a cloth pouch of attached files hanging at its axis.
scroll.codeAria: A sample skill: writing product captions in the brand voice
scroll.lampAria: Hand lantern: move it along the wall to light the scrolls’ name tags
scroll.pouchAria: Cloth pouch with the attached files (references/)

code.code:
---
name: product-caption
description: Write product captions in the brand voice. Use when you need a caption for Facebook, Instagram or TikTok.
---

# Product caption

## Steps
1. Ask for the product name, 3 highlights and the platform.
2. Read the brand voice in references/brand-voice.md.
3. Write 3 options: an opening line, a body under 60 words, a call to action.
4. Never promise what the product doesn't do; never use the word “best”.

## Example
In: Linen shirt, airy, low-crease, 3 colours
Out: 35 degrees outside and still light as a morning breeze. An airy, low-crease linen shirt in three soft colours…

notes.text: Name: lowercase, numbers, hyphens; same as the skill's folder name.
Description: what it does + when to use it. AI reads this line first to know when to open the scroll.
Steps: write them as if briefing a new hire, in order.
Attachments: long documents live separately; AI opens them only when needed.
A “don't” rule is a step too — say clearly what not to do.
An in → out example helps AI catch the voice fastest.

facts.text: Per the spec, SKILL.md must have a name and a description; the body holds instructions; it may include scripts, references and assets folders.
At first AI reads only each skill's name and description; it opens the whole scroll when a task fits (progressive disclosure).

insight.text: The description is the shop sign: AI reads it first and opens the scroll when a task fits — so state “when to use” clearly.

scroll.detail: The spec suggests keeping SKILL.md under 500 lines and moving long details to attached files. Each tool supports the standard differently — check your tool's docs.

moons.label: From habit to standard
moons.art: Ink painting: a rolling moss field under the moon seen from above at a slant; a worn trail enters at the bottom-left corner, swings in an S past six carved stone posts and fades into the mist in the middle of the horizon. Drag the moon along its ink arc: it waxes, the posts’ long shadows swing with it, and at each milestone a post lights up, the trail paves itself stone by stone and the words appear on the moss; today, many walk it with lanterns.
moons.prompt: Drag the moon past the milestones

fact.text: Anthropic announces MCP, an open standard for connecting AI assistants to data and tools.
Anthropic's guide separates workflows (fixed routes) from agents (choose their own steps) and advises starting simple.
GitHub open-sources Spec Kit: write a spec, plan, split into small checkable tasks, then let AI write code.
Anthropic launches Agent Skills: folders with a SKILL.md that Claude loads only when a task needs them.
Agent Skills is published as an open standard at agentskills.io so many tools can share it.
agentskills.io lists 40+ products supporting skills, from Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI to GitHub Copilot and Cursor.

horizon.text: Skills may become a common way to carry a workflow from one AI tool to another — not certain yet.

insight.text: In about a year, “teach AI once” went from one tool's trick to an open format many tools can read.

moons.detail: The agentskills.io list is the standard's own showcase page; the exact level of support in each tool may differ.

spec.label: Spec first, code later
spec.art: Ink painting: a thick plank workbench under a paper lamp, seen from above; a washi blueprint lies in the warm pool, its corners held by stones, eight pencil rings round its margin. Eight pebbles carved with the steps lie along the near edge; each one set in its ring changes the sheet: a sketch of the feeling, question marks, a block of spec, cut lines, then the pieces fold up into a paper workshop, a pine and a fence by a pond, with real shadows; at last it folds flat and rolls up into a skill hung on a hook.
spec.pathAria: An eight-step stone path: from a description to a skill
spec.keys: Tap in turn, or use number keys 1 to 8.
spec.done: The path is lit. Open your take-away card.
spec.hookAria: The skill you just saved, on its hook: open it on the bench

steps.label: Describe the feel you want
steps.detail: Tell it like you'd tell a friend: who uses it, what they see, how it should feel.
steps.why: AI needs to know the destination before choosing the road.

steps.label: Let AI ask back
steps.detail: Say: “ask me until it's clear; don't write code yet”.
steps.why: AI's questions expose what you haven't thought of.

steps.label: Write the spec as .md
steps.detail: Collect the answers in one file: goals, rules, limits, what counts as done.
steps.why: The spec is a shared blueprint; you and AI look at one page.

steps.label: Split into phases
steps.detail: Cut it into small tasks, each one checkable on its own.
steps.why: Small tasks are easy to check; mistakes stay small.

steps.label: Hand each part to a coding agent
steps.detail: Claude Code, Codex or a similar tool does one phase at a time.
steps.why: One task at a time keeps the agent on track.

steps.label: Check with screenshots and numbers
steps.detail: Take screenshots, measure speed, click through it like a user.
steps.why: What you can see and measure needn't be guessed.

steps.label: Fix the exact spot
steps.detail: Say clearly: what you expected, what you saw, on which screen.
steps.why: A clear bug report lets AI fix it without breaking other things.

steps.label: Save it as a skill
steps.detail: A method that worked well → write it up as a SKILL.md.
steps.why: Next time call the skill instead of explaining from scratch.

facts.text: GitHub calls this spec-driven development: intent comes first, AI does small tasks, a person reviews each step.

insight.text: The spec is a shared blueprint: say clearly what you want once, AI builds part by part, you check each part.

spec.detail: Tool names are only examples. This works with any coding agent that reads Markdown files.

line.label: The workshop line
line.art: Ink painting: a long plank corridor in the workshop at night, converging on the far door open to a bright moon garden. Eight paper lanterns hang on an ink cord, near ones large and warm, far ones small and cool, each throwing a pool of light on the floor and the paper walls; each station’s name is written on its lantern. In front, a low table with a bowl of vermilion stones and a brush resting on an inkstone. Join the lanterns with a brush stroke and set vermilion stones under the ones that need a person.
line.task: Example: a new product goes on the shelf
line.stoneAria: Set a red stone — a human reviewer — at {name}

stations.name: Pick the one to use
stations.why: Picking needs taste and knowing the brand.

stations.name: Check rights & AI label
stations.why: Getting rights or labels wrong is a legal risk.

stations.name: Schedule the post
stations.why: Once posted, it's hard to take back.

line.extraStone: A red stone here is fine too — but slower, without adding safety.
line.missingStone: {n} spot(s) still need a human reviewer and have no red stone.
line.done: The line runs: machines do the repetitive parts, you keep the three that matter.

facts.text: Anthropic's guidance: agents should pause at checkpoints for human feedback; human review stays very important.

insight.text: Automate the repetitive parts; put a human in the loop where taste, rights or no-undo actions are involved.

line.detail: Links to station 15: for sending, paying or deleting data, have the agent stop and ask you.
